title: OR-D-03 callback reverse-mapping hijack: fixed in source, live testnet kernel still vulnerable
description: The uniqueness guard now exists in source: PutMiniApp asserts CallbackIndexMap[callbackContract] is null or already equals the same appId ("callback already registered", MorpheusOracle.Storage.cs:270-275), the stale-mapping delete is owner-checked (Storage.cs:258-262), and RebuildIndexes is admin-gated, bounded and first-wins/idempotent (MorpheusOracle.Requests.cs:153-183, guard at 174-178). However contracts/README.md:82-84 confirms the deployed testnet kernel 0xf54d8584ef82315c1800373272ab08ae0db2d5ef predates this fix: on the live chain any account can still register a fresh appId over another app's callback contract and repoint its legacy request routing (last-write-wins), a permissionless routing takeover / DoS against RequestFromCallback / Request / QueueAutomationRequest flows (MorpheusOracle.cs:1057-1094 resolve apps via FindMiniAppByCallback).
recommendation: Ship the pending ContractManagement.Update carrying the source fix to testnet (and verify mainnet kernel hash against the same source before/after upgrade), then run RebuildIndexes to backfill the reverse index; until deployed, treat callback-based routing on 0xf54d8584 as untrusted and prefer appId-direct SubmitMiniAppRequest paths.

title: ExpireStaleRequest inbox gap: fixed in source, live kernel still leaves inbox empty on expiry
description: Source now stores a canonical failed InboxItem and emits OnMiniAppInboxStored on expiry (MorpheusOracle.cs:842-861), matching the FulfillRequest shape (1151-1165). The deployed kernel (per contracts/README.md:93-96) refunds and emits RequestExpired/MiniAppRequestCompleted but writes no inbox item, so consumers that only poll GetInboxItem never observe the terminal state and wait indefinitely. No funds at risk (refund path is symmetric and clamped to the accrued pool, 802-822; sponsored-spend release at 831-834; reserved-fee release at 840); impact is consumer availability/liveness only, with a documented workaround (poll GetRequest().Status).
recommendation: Include in the same ContractManagement.Update as the OR-D-03 fix; until then document/enforce that consumers treat GetRequest().Status as the source of truth for terminal states.

title: Storage-prefix layout footgun: decimal-counted hex literals frozen on-chain
description: The prefix allocation block (MorpheusOracle.cs:64-93, definitions 94-143) documents that early prefixes were advanced as if counting in decimal (0x09 -> 0x10, 0x19 -> 0x20), leaving 0x0A-0x0F and 0x1A-0x1F skipped-but-free. Current assignments (0x01-0x2C) are collision-free in source, but the layout is frozen for the deployed contracts: any future edit that renumbers an existing prefix, or a contributor misreading the gaps as reserved, orphans live on-chain keys. Risk is process-level (upgrade-time data corruption), not an active bug.
recommendation: Keep the FOOTGUN comment; enforce append-only prefix allocation in review, add a source-assertion test pinning the full prefix map (alongside existing ContractSourceAssertions tests), and have the planned platform-library refactor reuse this exact map rather than re-deriving prefixes.

title: Keystore error swallow fixed; residual silent-fallback + ephemeral-key gate can still rotate oracle key without alarm
description: The original bug (empty catch {} silently regenerating the oracle key on a malformed keystore) is fixed: loadStableOracleKeyMaterial now returns undefined only on ENOENT and throws on invalid JSON or any other read/decrypt error (crypto.js:225-238), and ephemeral key generation is hard-gated behind MORPHEUS_ALLOW_EPHEMERAL_KEY (default false -> throws, crypto.js:574-578). Residual: the outer resolution chain still swallows parse/decrypt errors from both the configured-key path (catch at 560-565) and the stable-keystore path (catch at 567-572) with no log or metric, so if MORPHEUS_ALLOW_EPHEMERAL_KEY=true is ever set in a deployment, keystore corruption silently rotates the oracle encryption key - in-flight sealed payloads become undecryptable and the on-chain OracleEncryptionPublicKey drifts from the live key with no operator signal.
recommendation: Log (and metric/alert) at warn level inside both fallback catches including the original error; add a startup check that refuses MORPHEUS_ALLOW_EPHEMERAL_KEY=true outside explicit dev mode; keep the production env examples showing the flag unset/false.

title: Sandbox production enforcement keys on NODE_ENV, which no deployment config sets - guard is inert in the enclave
description: Both runners fork user-supplied JS/WASM children and honor SCRIPT_CHILD_ENABLE_PERMISSION_MODEL=false by dropping all --permission flags (script-runner.js:23-24, wasm-runner.js:23-24). The intended production guard (validateChildProcessPermissions, permission-guard.js:95-100, called from script-runner.js:21 and wasm-runner.js:21) only throws when process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production'. Grep across workers/nitro-worker/Dockerfile, deploy/nitro/Dockerfile.enclave, entrypoint-*.sh, docker-compose*.yml and all .env*.example files finds NODE_ENV set nowhere, so in the real Nitro enclave the guard never fires: anyone controlling enclave env (the host operator - a nominally untrusted party in the TEE threat model - or a config mistake) can run untrusted scripts with full child-process permissions inside the enclave that also holds oracle key material. Partial mitigation: SCRIPT_CHILD_ALLOW_NET wildcards/CIDRs are rejected unconditionally (permission-guard.js:102-111) and child env is scrubbed to PATH/TZ (script-runner.js:81-84).
recommendation: Invert the guard to default-deny: refuse SCRIPT_CHILD_ENABLE_PERMISSION_MODEL=false unless an explicit dev flag (e.g. MORPHEUS_SANDBOX_DEV_MODE=true) is set, independent of NODE_ENV; and/or set NODE_ENV=production in the enclave Dockerfile/entrypoint. Add a startup self-check that forks a probe child asserting fs/net denials before serving traffic (noted as a test gap in .planning/codebase/CONCERNS.md).

title: VRF randomness generated by relayer-local crypto.randomBytes when enclaveFulfill flag is off (the live default)
description: The random.generate lane short-circuits to crypto.randomBytes(32) on the host relayer (executor.js:307-326, route 'local:vrf') whenever config.nitro.enclaveFulfill is false; the enclave-attested path behind it (executor.js:287-305, POST /oracle/fulfill) is flag-gated Phase-4 and off in the live box (config.js:431-438; corroborated by claudedocs/oracle-lane-validation-2026-06-15.json and deploy/nitro/enclave-server.mjs comments). The value is not bound to requestId, block, or any commit-reveal scheme: the relayer operator observes the outcome before broadcasting and, with host access, can patch or re-roll between generation and checkpoint. The normal retry path does persist the first prepared fulfillment (checkpointPreparedFulfillment, delivery.js:93-128), which prevents naive cross-tick re-rolling. trust_tier is truthfully labeled host-unattested (enclave.js:37-38), but the on-chain FulfillRequest carries the same pinned-verifier ECDSA signature either way (MorpheusOracle.cs:1132-1135), so on-chain consumers cannot distinguish enclave-attested VRF from host randomness - games of chance requesting random.generate on N3 today receive host-generated randomness under an oracle-verifier signature.
recommendation: Gate the local:vrf lane behind an explicit config opt-in (e.g. allowHostVrf, default false) so random.generate fails closed until enclaveFulfill ships; bind VRF output to requestId+contract+network inside the enclave path; surface trust_tier in the on-chain inbox/result metadata or docs so consumers can reject unattested randomness; until then, warn games-of-chance integrations in docs that VRF is host-trusted.

title: Durable-intake invariant degrades to local-state-only during transient Supabase insert failures
description: The normal path honors persist-before-cursor-advance (request-processor.js:201 before last_block write at 218-219; request-id lane 108 before 115-116), failClosed defaults to on (config.js:359) so a fully-unavailable Supabase throws and the cursor is not advanced, and cross-instance claims fail closed during backoff by default (queue.js:332-341, config.js:368-371). However persistFreshEventsToDurableQueue catches transient insert errors and merely warns (queue.js:296-301) - that tick's events are then processed and the block cursor advances with only the local state file as durability. The circuit breaker (markSupabasePersistenceUnavailable via isTransientDurableQueueError, queue.js:252-253) makes subsequent ticks fail closed, bounding exposure to the first failing tick; a relayer crash plus local state-file loss inside that window would skip those events permanently.
recommendation: Treat first-failure ticks as fail-closed for the cursor (throw after logging so the discovery catch skips the advance), or spool failed intake events to a local append-only journal that is replayed before the cursor may advance; alert on the 'continuing with local relayer state' warn so operators know the durable lane is degraded.
